text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish newspapers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Grain trade slowed considerably at the end of last year and producers have half of last year's crop in store. Before Finland joined the EU, the state would have bought the surplus but this is no longer possible.
- A technical failure and crew inability to use emergency tools took Silja's Silja Europa aground in the Stockholm archipelago two years ago, inquiry shows. @
- Finnish auditing firms expand into consulting, expecting know-how of mergers and acquisitions and financing to bring more profitable accounts than auditing.
- Pressure is increasing to harmonise all indirect taxation in the European Union, but Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says he does not believe full harmonisation is necessary.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Competition will be fierce between pulp derivatives exchanges. Finnish SOP's pulp bourse the first to start next week, but London's Pulpex and Liverpool Livedex to open this spring and Chicago Mercantile Exchange may also list pulp. @
- Merita trying to settle case on construction firm Haka's activities in the U.S. which could cost up to 650 million markka if no settlement is reached.
- Finnish venture capital investment surged last year to 504 million markka from 225 million markka in 1995.
DEMARI
- NATO membership is not a goal for Finland, neither should it be an obligation to every western country, President Martti Ahtisaari says in an interview to an Italian newspaper. @
- A third of voters who did not vote in local elections last year say there was no suitable candidate.
- Former Finnish missionary in Japan Martti Turunen, trying to win a seat in the Japanese upper house of parliament, changes spelling of his name to 'Marutei Tsurunen'.
AAMULEHTI

- Chancellor of justice Jorma S. Aalto has not found evidence that second finance minister Arja Alho did anything to jeorpardise Finland's interests in connection with linking the markka to ERM in October last year. @
- Racing reindeer to undergo doping tests.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Environmental activists in Turku demand free public transport and a ban on private cars for cleaner air.
